chapter_title: The Apostle is asked: Why when you drew every thing in the Picture (- Book), did you not draw the Purification of the Catechumens who shall be cleansed by Transmigration?
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by dialogue frame plus late soteriological/institutional concerns (catechumen vs elect) and Christianized eschatological vocabulary (Judge, gehenna, eternal rest). No stable cosmos→cosmos correspondential exposition appears; the explanation of transmigration remains schematic and is anchored to church categories, consistent with the strong editorial-fatigue/pastoral drift in the second half.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic narrative setup (“Once again…”, “our enlightener…”) introducing a catechumen’s question; pure dialogue frame.

Eschatological reward/punishment in Christianized terms (notably “gehenna”, “Judge”, forensic trial language). This reads as material entering via Jewish/Christian eschatological vocabulary rather than an internal cosmological mapping.
Continues the same Christianized eschatological register (“place of rest for ever”, “brought before the Judge”), framed as a catechumen’s plea; no systematic cosmological mechanics are taught here.

Marked by explicit institutional categories (“catechumen”, “elect”) and a practical explanation about why the catechumen’s route cannot be depicted; the opening dialogue attribution (“Then speaks…”) is also late frame, but the paragraph’s substance is an institutional/applied rationale rather than substrate cosmology.

Institutional soteriology focused on the catechumen’s ‘middle way’ of purification versus the elect; the concern is operational/classificatory (how/where purification happens), not a cosmos→cosmos correspondential structure.
Formulaic closing response (“heard… was persuaded… kept silent”), typical of the editorial dialogue frame.
